description:
Design a 3D model of ambidextrous scissors for Helping Hands.

The user wants scissors that work comfortably and effectively in either the left or right hand. Develop a plausible mechanical concept and an editable 3D model, not merely symmetric handles on an otherwise handed pair of scissors. Investigate how blade overlap, pivot preload, grip forces, and visibility of the cut affect use in either hand. Consider a reversible arrangement or another practical mechanism, and choose an approach based on feasibility and usability rather than assuming one mechanism is required.

Use suitable CAD/modeling tools. Provide the editable source model, useful exchange/export files, and rendered views or an animation showing operation in both hands. Explain the chosen mechanism, assembly, materials, tolerances, and what would need physical prototyping to validate cutting performance. Distinguish a conceptual or printable fit prototype from a proven working cutting tool; do not claim the model alone demonstrates reliable cutting.

The request was spoken as “a 3 d marker of ambidextrous scissors,” interpreted in context as a 3D model. This pebble is for the Helping Hands project. Follow the project's established artifact and design workflow. File this work for later; do not implement it in the current voice conversation.
